title: feat(plugin-security, runtime, core)!: the permission-set grant, clone and activation doors take a package, and a grant is unique per package
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-bill"} -->
_Requested by **Bill** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wg?thread=cmsg_016iMXWSZDzqWRWvWzdNo8wgUk6E2cvLTcMKqA8wHeFGpu)_

domain:server#2 · os-bill · session_01Utp6CaP1iy4RSEQbW6177G

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么：给用户授权权限集、开关权限集（激活入口）、克隆权限集这三个入口，现在都能用 `permission_set_package` / `?package=` 指明“哪个包的那一个”；同名权限集由两个包持有时，不指明包就拒绝（409）并列出候选包。授权的唯一键加上了包这一列；不带包的授权仍是一人、一个权限集、一个组织只有一条，由上一段（P1b，已合入）建好的守卫保证；同一用户在同一组织里对同一权限集仍只能有一条授权（两个包各一条除外），由引擎里的写入缝把关，拒绝时与旧键的回答一致。权限集的开关台账按“包 + 名字”各占一行，开关一个包的不会碰另一个包的。
- 为什么改：ADR-0150 允许两个包各有一个同名权限集（#31698 PR-2 之后才真正出现），而这三个入口原来只按名字找，遇到同名要么答“不存在”（404/400），要么存错包。本 PR 是 #32164 三段里的最后一段（P1 与 P1b 已合入 main），落地后 PR-2 才能放开同名。
- 风险与回滚：属于收窄（BREAKING，标题带 `!`）。只有一个包持有时，三个入口的回答与 main 一致：17 项回答的 md5 在本轮代码上重测，与上一轮对照 main 入口源码时的结果逐字节相同，2 项灵敏度对照照样不同。唯一的例外已在 changeset 写明：环境自建且被覆盖层改过的权限集，开关入口写的台账行不再带 `sys_metadata` 标记而是空包，各读者对两者读法相同。收紧六处：指明一个并不持有该权限集的包会 409（以前静默改写或照存）；建议记录指明建议包够不着的持有者会 409；两个入口只认 `package` 查询参数，其它参数回 400；克隆目标名若被两个包持有算已占用；同名多行台账里有不带包的行时开回会 409；AI 服务账号的权限天花板改按授权所指的那个包来判，判不出是哪个包时任一持有者越线即拒（后两处要到 #31698 PR-2 之后才会出现）。第一方没有任何调用会碰到。旧的三列唯一索引只在守卫建成后作为一次 safe 替换退役（本地在 MariaDB 10.11 与 PostgreSQL 16 实测），不会被当作孤儿索引删掉。回滚即还原本 PR，无数据迁移。上一轮补齐了契约复审（6813617327）和专题红线复审（6813516860）的全部条目，两份复审在 `ec39bd8e5` 上都已通过（6817263634、6817314015）。本轮再补两处：一人一组的检查排到授权表其它拒绝之后，调用方读不到的持有者照旧答 `reference_not_found`；环境与某个包同名时，带 `sys_metadata` 哨兵的台账行认作环境自己那一行。另有一处声明过的先后变化：第二条授权若同时也过不了记录校验，以前答 400，现在答 409，两种情况都什么也不存。
- 先看：`packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/stored-permission-set-package-stamp.ts`（F3 拒绝 `assertNamedPackageHolds`，一人一组一权限集 `assertOneGrantPerSet`），然后 `packages/runtime/src/domains/catalog-activation.ts`（`?package=` 定址与按包的台账行）和 `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts`（唯一键）。
- 两分钟验证：`pnpm --filter @objectstack/runtime exec vitest run src/domains/permission-set-package-doors.test.ts`，预期 38 条全过：两个包持有时不带包回 409 并带两个候选；`?package=` 指 HR 回 200，只写 HR 自己的台账行，CRM 的行不动。
- 需要你做的：无。改动共 2920 行，没有碰到受治理的路径（`check-governed-merges --branch` 判定 0/51）。按现行规则，契约复审和专题红线复审由席位来跑，通过后由席位落地。

Fixes #32164

Clause-②: no (narrowing)
- Widening, at the grant, clone and activation doors: a permission set two packages hold, addressed with no package: FROM read as absent (the grant's `400 reference_not_found`, the clone and activation doors' `404`) TO `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming the holders; addressed with a package that holds it (`permission_set_package` on the grant, `?package=` on clone and activation): FROM the package dropped TO exactly that package's set.
- Widening, the grant's unique key: FROM one grant per `(user_id, permission_set, organization_id)` TO one per `(user_id, permission_set, permission_set_package, organization_id)`, so one user may hold both packages' sets of one name in one organization. A grant naming no package stays one per `(user_id, permission_set, organization_id)` through the guard the preceding PR builds, except on `driver-memory` (declared below).
- Narrowing (F3), a named package that does not hold the set, at any holder count: FROM the grant or audience-binding suggestion re-stamped to the holder (one holder) or stored with no package (two holders), a system column-only bind landing as written, and `?package=` dropped at the clone and activation doors (one holder: the holder's set) TO `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, reason `not-held-by-qualifier`, naming the holders, with nothing stored or switched.
- Narrowing, an audience-binding suggestion naming a holder outside the reach of the package that made it (not that package, a dependency or a kernel package): FROM re-stamped by the rule's answer (no package) TO `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, reason `outside-closure`, naming that holder, nothing stored.
- Narrowing, the agent-account ceiling (ADR-0151 D3) for a set two packages hold: FROM read by the bare name, which the rule refuses, so no breach was found and the grant or position was admitted TO the set the row would hold (the grant's own package, a position's sets from the package that declared it) judged, and a read the rule still refuses judging every holder of the name: a breach of any refuses the write.
- Narrowing, the query sets are closed: FROM any query parameter dropped without a word TO `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` before any lookup, at the clone door and at the activation door for all six of its types (`position`, `permission`, `sharing_rule`, `webhook`, `queue`, `assignment_rule`), for anything but `package` on `permission`, and for a repeated or blank `package`.
- Narrowing, a clone target name two packages hold: FROM free (the reader answers nothing for a refused name, so the copy was saved) TO taken, `409`, as a name one package holds already was.
- Narrowing, the activation ledger for a permission set two packages hold: switching a holder on while a ledger row naming no package, or naming a package that no longer serves the name, keeps it off: FROM (reachable only after #31698 PR-2) that row re-addressed to the holder, which re-armed the other holder too TO `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` naming that row, nothing written (ADR-0150 red line 1). The same with one holder when the name has more than one row, which no first-party writer makes. A disabled package still holds the name here, as the rule counts it.
- Moved, refused either way: a second grant of one set to one user in one organization whose row record validation would also refuse: FROM `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` (the store's key answered after validation) TO the one-grant check's `409`, nothing stored either way. Every refusal of the grant table's hooks, and the engine's answer for a holder the caller cannot read, keep their precedence.

Metadata-protocol: none

Skills-docs: follow-up #32539 (skills/objectstack-data/rules/security.md: its grant paragraph still says one grant per user, set and organization is "enforced by the `unique: 'organization'` index"; after this PR the key is `(user_id, permission_set, permission_set_package, organization_id)` with the package-less guard and the engine's one-grant check, and a grant may name `permission_set_package`. This lane does not edit `skills/**`.)

**BREAKING** for a writer that sends `permission_set_package` naming a package that does not hold the permission set (or, on a suggestion, a holder outside the suggesting package's reach), and for a request carrying a query parameter to the clone door or to the activation door, for any of its six types. No first-party writer or caller meets any of the narrowings: the boot backfill and `os migrate stored-references bind` write only a holder, and the Console sends no query to these doors. Every moved answer, door by door, is in the changeset.

This is the last of three PRs for #32164. P1 (#32356, `48d6b477c7`) taught `driver-sql`'s widening arm the superseded grant key's 18.0, shadow-carried and not-yet-physical forms; P1b (#32357, `e765a092`) builds the grant's package-less guard at schema sync on every kernel that runs the table's DDL. Both are on `main`, and this branch carries `main` merged (`371bd8d45`), so the diff here is P2's own: 51 files, +2748 / -172 (2920 lines). Opened by `domain:server#3` (os-support-ai); continued by `domain:server#2`.

## What changes

- **The grant** (`plugin-security`): `grant-permission-set-name.ts` judges a non-system writer's grant through the security catalog by `(package, name)` (`judgeGrantSet`): a set two packages hold, named with no package, is refused with core's `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` (`RESOURCE_CONFLICT`, 409, the D3 sentence, `.refusal.candidates`); a named holder is kept; a named non-holder is refused (`not-held-by-qualifier`). `stored-permission-set-package-stamp.ts` keeps a named package that holds the set for every writer and refuses one that does not (`assertNamedPackageHolds`), on insert, on update and on a column-only bind, for the grant and for `sys_audience_binding_suggestion`; it never re-stamps a named package. Before the boot seals the holders, a system insert's named package is kept unjudged (the backfill reads a stale one as none). The `sys_metadata` overlay provenance sentinel reads as no package, as core's `catalogEntryAddress` reads it. On a suggestion (R3) a named holder must be in the suggesting package's reach (itself, its dependencies, the kernel packages), else `409 outside-closure`.
- **One grant of a set per user and organization** (`plugin-security`, the same seam, `assertOneGrantPerSet`): the two keys alone do not refuse every second grant of one set to one user in one organization that the old key refused, so the seam judges each grant insert, and each update that moves its user, set, organization or package, reading the other grants of that user, set and organization as the system in the writer's transaction. It admits a second grant only when the two name two different packages that each hold the set, and otherwise refuses with the engine's own duplicate-record envelope (`DUPLICATE_RECORD`, 409; `409 UNIQUE_VIOLATION`, "A record with this value already exists", on the wire), the answer the old key gave. The check is its own pair of hooks at priority 50, after every refusal of the grant table's hooks (the set's name 30, the agent ceiling set 35, the holder's membership 40, the AI service account's ceiling 45), so those keep their answer; and, as they do, it steps aside for a non-system write on a holder the write names that the caller's own read does not return, which the engine's reference check answers as a user that does not exist (#29029; `holderLeftToReferenceCheck`, now exported by `grant-holder-membership-refusal.ts`). Record validation runs after every hook, so a second grant it would also refuse answers `409` where `main` answered `400` (declared). Below the engine, a race, a batch and a write with no organization stay with the keys (declared in the changeset). The boot backfill (`stored-permission-set-package-backfill.ts`) catches a per-row unique violation, leaves that row with no package and reports it as `duplicated`, so the walk goes on; a dry run asks the check's own predicate and reports the same rows as `duplicated`, not `bound`.
- **The agent-account ceiling** (`plugin-security`, `agent-account-grant-refusal.ts`, ADR-0151 D3): the set an AI service account would hold is read as the authorization resolver reads it, a grant at its stored package and a position's sets from the position's package; a read the rule still refuses judges every holder of the name and fails closed.
- **The activation door** (`runtime`, `catalog-activation.ts`): `?package=PKG` addresses exactly PKG's set. The permission ledger store is addressed by `(package, name)` (`addressing: 'package-and-name'`, scoped to `permission`): each holder keeps its own row, so switching one holder's set never touches the other's. Two holders and no package answer `409` with `details.candidates`; a non-holder is `409 not-held-by-qualifier`; switching a holder on while a package-less or stale row keeps it off is `409` naming that row, nothing written; a write that would re-address a row switched off for another holder is refused. With one holder, a package or the environment, the name's only row is the holder's and the write takes it over, as on `main`. Holders are counted as the D3 rule counts them, a disabled package included. Where the environment holds the name beside a package, the name alone is the environment's set, so a row stamped with the overlay provenance `sys_metadata` is the environment's own switch and is re-addressed by id to name no package, never doubled (epic read 6817314015, S1); the refusal's sentence for a package-less row now says when it switches off every holder (the bare name refused). The query set is closed (`package`, for `permission` only). Every other type keeps the name-addressed store.
- **The clone door** (`runtime`, `permission-set-clone.ts`): `?package=` names the SOURCE's package (the body's `package` still names where the copy lands); two holders and no package answer `409` with `details.candidates`; a target name two packages hold is taken; the query set is closed.
- **core** (`security-catalog.ts`): the refused arm of `SecurityCatalogResolution` gains an optional `holders`, the candidates structured, so a door can answer them without re-deriving. Additive.
- **The grant's key** (`objects/sys-user-permission-set.object.ts`): `(user_id, permission_set, organization_id)`, `unique: 'organization'` → `(user_id, permission_set, permission_set_package, organization_id)`, `unique: 'global'`. The package-less guard P1b builds keeps grants that name no package to one per `(user_id, permission_set, organization_id)`; the old three-column index retires only once the guard stands, through `driver-sql`'s widening arm (P1) as one `safe` replace. A store whose old key is carried by a hash shadow (MySQL, MariaDB) keeps it, declared in the changeset with the remedy by hand.
- **`metadata-protocol`**: the guard migration's module doc states the grant's declared key as this change makes it (a comment; no code).
- Docs: `content/docs/permissions/permission-sets.mdx` (the grant's package, the clone door's `?package=`, the `driver-memory` limit), `authorization.mdx` (the activation door's `?package=` and the per-package ledger rows), `system-context.mdx` rows 23c and 23h (the stamp's system column bind, the grant's 409 refusals and the one-grant check's system read; the generated site register regenerated). QA: `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/access-security.json`, item `access-security.security-catalog-activation-and-clone-doors` revision 4 (the closed query and the two-holder arms).

## Why

ADR-0150 D3/D4/D5/D8, a child of #31527 ahead of #31698 PR-2. Once two packages can each hold a permission set of one name, a door that addresses a set by bare name must either be told which one or refuse naming both; a grant must record which one it grants, and the grant's key must let one user hold both. These doors answered a two-holder name as absent (404, or the grant's 400 `reference_not_found`) and dropped `?package=`, and a grant's named package was re-stamped rather than judged.

Rulings applied: seat 3's F1 (`?package=` on the POST doors; clone's names the source), F2 (an additive `holders` in core; structured candidates on `/data` are #32250) and F3 (a named non-holder refused at any holder count, a column-only bind included); the epic seat's M5 conditions (comment 6770072902) and its two rulings after the first contract review (comment 6774878772): the permission ledger keyed by package with the refusal kept as a backstop, and condition 1 closed at schema sync (landed in P1b).

## Tests

- `plugin-security/src/grant-permission-set-package.test.ts` (new, 19): a real `ObjectQL` over SQLite with the grant-name hook and the stamp seam registered as the plugin registers them, over a stand-in registry holding one set in two packages. Two holders: no package is 409 with both candidates (envelope and `/data` wire), a holder is stored, a non-holder is 409; F3: one holder with another package named, an environment-only set with a package named, and a column-only bind; updates: an echo, a non-system package value, a rename; the overlay sentinel. CONTROLs: one holder, no package or the holder, stored stamped; a name nothing holds stays `400 reference_not_found`. [E2] The seam's refusal of a second grant equals the store's own unique violation, envelope and wire (measured against the four-column key with the seam's reads off), at the data door too; two holders' sets once each are stored.
- `plugin-security/src/stored-permission-set-package-backfill.test.ts`: F3 on `sys_audience_binding_suggestion` (insert and column-only update naming a non-holder: 409, nothing stored), and a system insert naming a package for an unheld name after the seal (kept as written). [E2] One grant of a set per user and organization at the seam: beside a package-less row or a stale one (one holder), the same package twice and a package-less grant beside a packaged one (two holders), a column-only bind and a move to another user are refused with nothing written; CONTROL: other users, organizations and sets, and an update that keeps the key. The backfill reports a row whose bind would duplicate as `duplicated`, leaves it null and binds the next row, with and without the seam. [SF3] A suggestion naming a holder outside the suggester's reach is `409 outside-closure` on insert and update; its own and a dependency's are kept.
- `plugin-security/src/agent-account-grant-refusal.test.ts` [E3]: two holders of one name, one above the ceiling: a grant naming the breaching package is refused and the other admitted, an update keeps the stored package, a grant whose read is refused fails closed (CONTROL: admitted when neither breaches), a position is judged on its own package's set.
- Per driver, the store alone [E2]: `metadata-protocol`'s guard suites (SQLite, live PostgreSQL 16, live MySQL / MariaDB) and `driver-memory`'s pin assert that the store alone admits a packaged grant beside a package-less one, where the old key refused it, so a later guard turns them red; Mongo's real-server suite carries the same rows, pinned, not run.
- `plugin-security/src/granted-by-writer-provenance.test.ts` and `grant-permission-set-name.test.ts`: pins that encoded the re-stamp now assert F3; the BASE answer is kept in comments. [E2] The without-guard CONTROL now asserts that the engine refuses a second package-less grant and that only a write below the engine lands one.
- `runtime/src/domains/permission-set-package-doors.test.ts` (new, 38): both doors through `HttpDispatcher.handleSecurity` over the real catalog reader. Two holders: 409 with structured candidates; `?package=` a holder addresses exactly that set (activation writes that holder's own ledger row, clone copies it into its pair); each holder keeps its own row and both stay independently switchable; a package-less or stale row keeps both off and switching one on is 409; a non-holder is 409; closed query sets are 400; a two-holder target is taken. CONTROLs: one holder answers as before, a legacy package-less or stale row is the one holder's switch, a position row is re-attributed by name as before. [E1] The environment as the one holder, plain and overlay: a stale row and a `sys_metadata` row are taken over on enable and disable; with no row, a disable writes one naming no package. [SF2] A disabled second holder still counts: the bare name is 409 naming both, a package-less row keeps the served holder off (409), and `?package=` the disabled one names the served holder. [S1] A package and the environment hold one name, the environment's set plain and overlay: a sentinel row is the environment's switch on enable and on disable (re-addressed, never a second row); CONTROL: `?package=` the package writes its own row and leaves the sentinel row alone.
- Round 3 [should-fix A]: `grant-holder-membership-refusal.test.ts`, a holder the caller cannot read that already holds the set gets one answer in every store, the reference refusal at `user_id`, on insert and on an update that moves a grant onto it (CONTROL: a holder the caller reads gets the `409`); `agent-account-grant-refusal.test.ts`, a second grant of a breaching set to an AI service account is the ceiling's `400` on insert and on a move (CONTROL: within the ceiling, the check's `409`); `stored-permission-set-package-backfill.test.ts`, a dry run reports the would-be second grant as `duplicated`.
- `core/src/security/security-catalog.test.ts`: `holders` on a refusal, in candidate order.
- Dogfood: `stored-reference-package-column.dogfood.test.ts`'s forged-column CONTROL asserts the engine now refuses the forge (F3) and writes it below the engine; `upgrade-18x-index-equivalence.dogfood.test.ts` pins the grant index's retirement on the restored 18.0 store as one safe replace.

## Acceptance notes

- **Two-holder answers are unreachable on a real registry until #31698 PR-2**, so every two-holder test uses a stand-in registry; every one-holder answer is what a real environment answers today, and the md5 CONTROL below holds the measured ones byte-identical to `main`'s door source (the environment's overlay row is the declared exception).
- **Structured candidates on `/data`** are #32250: the grant's refusal there carries the D3 sentence naming every holder, and the thrown error carries `.refusal.candidates`.
- **driver-memory, a declared limit.** It builds no package-less guard (no raw-SQL seam; the activation ledger's guard has the same exemption). Its unique check treats a NULL as distinct, so the driver alone admits two package-less grants of one set for one user in one organization where the old key refused the second; through the engine the one-grant check refuses the second, as on every driver. `memory-user-permission-set-packageless.test.ts` asserts the driver's own admission, so a future guard there turns it red on purpose.
- **Upgrading SQL databases.** The old index keeps refusing what it refused until a sync that runs safe drift (dev `autoMigrate: 'safe'`, or `os migrate apply`) replaces it, after the guard stands. On an 18.0 database that index is in the NULL-safe COALESCE form: retired only on a certified table and kept everywhere else (P1). A MySQL or MariaDB store whose old key is carried by a hash shadow keeps the three-column key; the changeset gives the `ALTER TABLE` that retires it by hand once the guard stands (P1 keeps the carrier and offers nothing, never an orphan drop).
- **The ceiling's fail-closed read judges the holders the catalog serves** (epic read 6817314015, S2): a disabled package's breaching set is not judged there, the same answer `main` gives for one holder, and the clamp at evaluation still holds. Carried by #32600 (blocked by this PR).
- **A real mongod was not run** (Verification): no CI lane runs the driver-mongodb real-server suites, and this container could not obtain a mongod binary.

Every suite ran under `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh`, which excludes other locked runs only, so no wall-clock figure here is an idle-box reading. The workspace was rebuilt after the merge (`turbo run build`, 119 tasks).

  - `@objectstack/runtime`: 586 files; 11283 passed, 19 skipped.
  - `@objectstack/plugin-auth`: 264 files; 4874 passed, 10 skipped (the first-party grant writers).
  - `@objectstack/core`: 153 files, 3429 passed.

Earlier rounds, unchanged code: E1, the sole-holder take-over (6); should-fix 2, the rule's holder count (1); E2, the one-grant check (4), the backfill's per-row catch (2) and the check's own-id exclusion (1); E3, the grant's package read (3) and the fail-closed read (1); should-fix 3, the closure restriction (1).

**Gates.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` then `--ran` on `085991120`: 116 derived, 116 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, every one exit 0. Also run, exit 0 each: `check-published-list-mirrors`, `check:changeset-fixed`, `check:error-code-casing`, `check:filter-alias-parity`, `check:published-readme-exports`, `check:route-ledger-census`, `check-system-context-census`, `check:platform-checklist`, `check-commit-card-trailers --range origin/main..HEAD` and `check-governed-merges --branch` (0 of 51 paths governed; 2920 changed lines, under 3000).

Not in that table, and declared in the changeset: the row the activation door writes for an environment-authored overlay set names no package where `main` wrote `sys_metadata`; every reader reads both as no package.
